#837. 'We fell behind' - what does new San Siro deal mean for AC Milan and Inter?

Why time is running out for the iconic San Siro

When AC Milan and city rivals Inter jointly revealed the design of their planned new stadium on Thursday, one thing stood out in particular - the name.

The 71,500-seater arena the clubs aim to share from 2031 onwards, replacing the iconic San Siro, will be called the Generali Stadium.

Generali is an Italian insurance company, and the firm has agreed to pay about 650m euros (Â£542m) for naming rights through to 2052.

The length and value of the agreement makes it one of the most lucrative naming-rights deals in sports history.

Stadium naming rights are, of course, nothing new in elite football. The champions of England and Germany both play in arenas built in the 21st century that have always been known by their sponsors' name, and plenty more stadiums across the continent have been partly financed by revenue from naming rights.

But in recent years, some clubs have struggled to sell them.

It was thought that both Tottenham Hotspur and West Ham would look to sell the rights to their new stadiums' names, but as yet neither have. Liverpool aimed to sell the name of a new stand they built in 2016 but no such deal has been agreed.

So, what do these stadium plans mean for AC Milan and Inter, what underpins the viability of expensive new football grounds, and what impact do culture and history have?

AC Milan and Inter are owned by separate US-based investment firms and in the joint announcement described the Generali Stadium as "a new home for generations of supporters, and a destination designed to contribute to the cultural, economic and urban development of the city".

The demolition of San Siro has been discussed for decades, and the clubs believe its deterioration and lack of modern features are significant reasons behind their progressive fall lower down the pecking order at the top of European football.

The new stadium is expected to cost about 1.2bn euros (Â£1bn) to construct, and the clubs aim to generate income by selling just under 12,000 of the seats as premium or hospitality, and host a wider array of events like concerts and fixtures in other sports.

"This is the biggest stadium naming-rights deal in the history of global sports," AC Milan owner Gerry Cardinale told BBC Sport.

"Thatâs a significant achievement in its own right and especially in the context of having been done in Italy and what it means to bring Italy back to the world stage of football.

"But if youâre looking at this purely as an annual sponsorship payment, youâre missing the bigger picture.

"The stadium is what fundamentally transforms our economic model - matchday revenues, hospitality, premium experiences, entertainment and commercial opportunities.

"These are the things that allow us to compete with the biggest clubs in Europe."

AC Milan have played at San Siro for 100 years, while Inter moved in 1947. The two clubs paid 197m euros (Â£164m) to buy the stadium and surrounding land in 2025.

The plans for the new stadium have faced opposition from some supporters, with some Inter fans protesting outside the venue where the plans were announced by carrying a banner reading 'You will never extinguish the lights at San Siro' and chanting "Hands off San Siro".

"You cannot compete consistently with the best clubs in the world without having the infrastructure and economic model to support that ambition," added Cardinale.

"The Premier League has set the benchmark in terms of commercial development and infrastructure. Italian football has fallen behind, and we need to change that.

"This stadium is a massive step forward, not just for AC Milan but potentially for the whole of Serie A."

The Generali Stadium will be built adjacent to San Siro, which will be knocked down once construction is complete

AC Milan v Inter and the tale of an iconic image

The two decades of naming rights paid for by Generali break down to about Â£27m per season - Â£13.5m per year, per club.

New stadiums are rarely built in Italy, with many Serie A stadiums in varying states of disrepair and in need of renovation before the country jointly hosts Euro 2032 with Turkey.

That means AC Milan and Inter have focused on selling a rare proposition.

"The 20-year deal is key - having that guaranteed long-term incomes gives the clubs security," said Dan Plumley - sport finance expert at Loughborough University.

"The money stacks up pretty well. Spotify pay around 20m euros (Â£17m) to sponsor Barcelona's Camp Nou per season, so now the Milan clubs aren't too far off that figure.

"What a lot of these partners are looking for is a long-term relationship because they can build their profile as expand around the world, pushing themselves into regions like Asia and Africa, and football can be very valuable for that.

"It couldn't be done at San Siro because everybody would have just carried on calling it that. Getting in early makes the sponsor part of the new history and is a really smart play from a business point of view."

The architects behind AC Milan and Inter's planned shared stadium saying it is designed to bring fans as close to the pitch as possible

Historically, the home of stadium naming rights has been the US, where the majority of arenas in most sports are known by a sponsor name.

In European football, similar deals have been most common in Germany, where major companies have direct ownership links to some of the country's biggest clubs including Bayer Leverkusen and Wolfsburg.

"It's really difficult to do naming-rights deals in English football because of our history and culture," said Plumley.

"The clubs and potential naming partners know that fans around the world could strongly oppose a deal, because it's less common here, so the value becomes less attractive."

Timing and performance on the pitch are key considerations when clubs are planning to sell the stadium name.

"As a club you don't want to just do a cheap deal and give the name away for a few million just because it's extra revenue," said Plumley.

"Clubs like Spurs or West Ham know there is a trade-off between not just agreeing something because it's a bit of extra value, having a deal that genuinely makes a difference financially, and doing something that the fans will tolerate.

"Sometimes the balance just isn't right, and some of the most successful clubs in the world would rather hold on and protect their overall value and hold off and sell when their performance is at its peak - being in the Champions League is key to that.

"Everton weren't in a position in terms of results to go out and get a big global name paying a huge amount every year, so a more local partner [the Hill Dickinson law firm] made sense."

#836. Michael J. Fox Shares Glimpse of Daughter Esme in Rare Photos

Michael J. Fox celebrated his and Tracy Pollan’s daughter Esme on her 25th birthday with sweet photos.

Michael J. Fox still has strong family ties.

The Back to the Future alum recently shared a peek as his and wife Tracy Pollan’s daughter Esme in honor of her 25th birthday.

“Ezzie, you’ve been many people over the last quarter century…all of them fabulous!” Fox wrote in a Nov. 3 Instagram post. “Happy birthday, I love you so much!”

In Fox’s post, he went back and forth from the future, including a photo of his daughter and wife from when she was a little kid, as well as highlights throughout her adulthood including her running the New York City Marathon and graduating from Duke University.

The 65-year-old’s sweet post comes shortly after Esme, as well as his and Pollan’s kids Sam, 37, and twins Aquinnah and Schuyler, both 31, joined him at the Emmys 2026 in September, where he was honored with the Bob Hope Humanitarian Award.

Fox emphasized the support he had received from his family throughout his Parkinson’s diagnosis, thanking them “for their sacrifices, for their patience, and for their love.”

He emphasized of everything his family had gone through since his 1991 diagnosis, “You have no idea.”

Meanwhile, Fox shared that he has been floored by the support he’s received from his audiences as his disease has progressed.

“Support from all of you who are so uplifting and just made me feel like I keep doing this,” he continued. “I hadn't lost what I do and you couldn't take it away from me. And it's because you stood up for me and I appreciate it. Eventually, I understood that accepting Parkinson's didn't mean I had to surrender to it. It just meant doing what I could for everyone living with this disease.”

Of course, Fox’s family has proved time and again that they will support him in his Parkinson’s journey—whether he is on or off the screen. In March, Esme and Schuyler ran the New York City Half Marathon in honor of her father’s eponymous foundation, which is fighting to find a cure to Parkinson’s.

“Congratulations to Schuyler, Esme, and all of the Team Fox runners for the love and effort they put into Sunday’s half marathon!” Fox wrote in a March Instagram post. “We’re so proud!”

#834. Hunger Games’ Mckenna Grace, Joseph Zada React to Fans Shipping Them

Sunrise on the Reaping stars Mckenna Grace and Joseph Zada shared their candid reaction to fans shipping them as a couple in real life: “It’s pretty weird.”

And if fans burn, they want the cast of The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping to burn with them.

Stars Joseph Zada and Mckenna Grace, however, are willing to take it all in stride. And by “it,” we mean fans taking their onscreen bond as Haymitch Abernathy and Maysilee Donner and hoping it becomes romantic IRL.

In reality, the concept made the pair laugh aloud when they were asked about being shipped in an interview.

“Yeah, it’s pretty weird,” Zada said with a smile to Refinery29 Australia, pointing out, “We’ve both got partners.”

He added that Grace feels like his “younger, younger sister,” which made the 20-year-old fire back at her costar, who is only a year older, “Younger? Definitely not.”

But while Zada and Grace may not have volunteered as ship tributes, Grace—who has long had her finger on the pulse of Gen Z internet trends—knows its par for the course in such a big franchise.

“Joe’s like family,” the Gifted star—who is dating her Regretting You costar Mason Thames—said. “I think that’s like the fun of the internet, is that they can ship whatever characters or people or anything that they want as long it’s not intruding on people’s own lives.”

Plus, Zada and Grace were willing to be more than just a piece in fans’ games, offering up alternative ships featuring their costars Ben Wang (who plays District 12 tribute Wyatt Callow), Laura Marcus (District 1 tribute Silka Sharp) and Whitney Peak (Haymitch’s love Lenore Dove).

As Zada noted, “I’ve been shipped with Ben, and like I can see that,” to which Grace added, “Honestly, my favorite ship is Ben and Joe.”

And when Zada suggested Marcus and Grace could also be a good ship, she offered up a challenge to her costar.

“I like Maydove,” she said, referring to her and Peak’s characters Maysilee and Lenore. “I’m coming for your girl.”

But not only does Grace have decades in the spotlight preparing her for this moment, but she also received advice from the boy with the bread, Josh Hutcherson, who played Peeta Mellark in the original movies and whom Grace starred alongside in Five Nights at Freddy’s 2.

As she revealed, Hutcherson was a wonderful sounding board as she prepared herself to step into the Hunger Games fandom.

“I just talk to Josh a lot because we were on that press tour together and spent a lot of time together,” she told E! News at the Coach Fall 2026 show on Feb. 11. “I spent a lot of time asking him, ‘Was your arena experience as intense as ours was?’ And he was like, ‘Oh yeah, yeah it was.’”

But while Zada and Grace have not dated, nor are they ever likely to, they’re not the only costars who have found themselves the subject of dating speculation. Read on for more costars whose relationships were strictly platonic—despite fans’ hopes to the contrary.

The Anyone But You costars may have found love onscreen, but that's where it stayed. Despite the onslaught of dating rumors amid their 2023 press tour, the pair emphasized that their relationship was strictly platonic.

"The two things that you have to sell a rom-com are fun and chemistry," Glen told the New York Times in April 2024. "Sydney and I have a ton of fun together, and we have a ton of effortless chemistry. That's people wanting what's on the screen off the screen, and sometimes you just have to lean into it a bit—and it worked wonderfully. Sydney is very smart."

Meanwhile, Sydney—who was engaged to businessman Jonathan Davino at the time, though they split in March 2025 after seven years together—asserted that she and Glen didn't play up their chemistry ahead of the rom-com's release.

"Honestly, the press did it themselves. There was no leaning in, per se," she told Variety in October 2025. "Truly, the tabloids and journalists just created it and kept going."

"Glen and I genuinely care for each other and have a love and respect for one another," she emphasized. "I love being with him. And I think people just truly saw a really beautiful pairing."

Hermione Granger and Draco Malfoy?! If Emma had it her way, the Harry Potter franchise would have had a Hogwarts House-crossed romance going down off-screen. The actress has admitted to nursing a serious crush on her bleached blonde co-star.During the Harry Potter 20th anniversary special, Emma shared that as a child she "fell in love" with Tom while on the set of their first film together, Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone. "I used to come in every day and look for his number on the call sheet, it was No. 7, and if his name was on the call sheet, it was an extra exciting day," she said during the reunion. "He was three years above me and so for him he was like, 'You're like my little sister.'"Shortly after the special premiered, fans of the series quickly took to the Internet to share their wish for the longtime friends to become something more.However, in an interview with British Vogue, Emma addressed the online reaction and put any potential dating rumors to rest. "We speak most weeks," she said, "and we just think it's sweet."

The one where Ross and Rachel were almost each other's lobsters in real-life.During HBO Max's Friends reunion last year, Jennifer and David, who played one of TV's most beloved couples, explained that art reflected real life a bit during the show's first season. "At some point, we were both crushing hard on each other, but it was like two ships passing because one of us was always in a relationship, and we never crossed that boundary," David said. "We respected that."Jennifer added, "Honestly, I remember saying one time to David, 'It's going to be such a bummer if the first time you and I actually kiss is going to be on national television.' And sure enough, the first time we kissed was in that coffee shop."So, instead of having a romance IRL, she explained that they "just channeled all of our adoration and love for each other into Ross and Rachel."

Arguably one of the most iconic pairings in movie history, fans have shipped Leo and Kate together since 1996's Titanic (even though she didn't make room for him on that door). Still, they never let go of their friendship, with Kate telling The Guardian last year that they are "bonded for life." From walking the red carpet together at the 1998 Golden Globes to watching DiCaprio blow kisses to Winslet during her emotional 2009 Golden Globes speech, it's so evident that the feelings between the besties have only continued to grow over the past two decades, iceberg be damned.

The unexpected pairing's chemistry in 2019's A Star Is Born and its ensuing press tour made fans blind to the fact that the actor and director was dating Irina Shayk and the pop star was engaged to Christian Carano at the time.Still, it was clear that the costars had a close bond, with Gaga revealing that she had an "instant connection" with Bradley that came "the second that I saw him."Of course, that closeness was on full display when the pair took to the Oscars stage in 2019, hand-in-hand, to perform their Best Song-winning number, "Shallow," just days after Gaga ended her engagement.

But the House of Gucci star quickly shut down romance rumors following the performance, telling Jimmy Kimmel, "Yes, people saw love and—guess what—that's what we wanted you to see."Bradley, whose romance with Irina ended later that year, never addressed the speculation until November 2021, telling The Hollywood Reporter they were acting during the Oscar performance."They kind of fall in love in that scene in the film," he explained. "It's that explosive moment that happens to them on a stage in front of thousands of people…It would have been so weird if we were both on stools facing the audience."

Since starring in Speed together in 1994, rumors have raced over the decades that Keanu and Sandra had an off-screen romance. Alas, it was never meant to me, with Sandra denying the two were ever a couple in an interview with Esquire magazine."Nope...but who knows?," she said. "Keanu's a guy who, I feel like, is friends with every woman he's ever dated. I don't think there's anyone who has something horrible to say about him. So maybe we could have survived. I don't know. But we didn't have to survive anything. We just get to grow up together on parallel roads and tip our hats and meet for a dinner and try to work together. And the longer time goes on, the more in awe I am of the human being. Would I have been able to say that if he had dumped me and made me angry? Probably not."Still, the duo, who also co-starred in 2006's The Lake House, are close friends, with Sandra citing Keanu's listening skills as one of his best attributes. The Miss Congeniality star recalled that about a year after filming Speed, she casually mentioned to her co-star that she'd never had champagne and truffles. A few days later, she told the outlet, Keanu hand-delivered those two items (and flowers), explaining, "I just thought you might want to try champagne and truffles, to see what it's like."

Moviegoers have Crazy, Stupid, Love for this pairing after they've played romantic interests in three films, including La La Land.Though they never dated in real life, working together forged a bond between the two actors. During a Q&A session at the 2018 Telluride Film Festival, the Cruella star revealed how much Ryan meant to her and his impact on her life and career. Calling him a "dear, wonderful friend," Emma said, "I can't even imagine what my life would be without Ryan. She then added, "He's so special. It makes me emotional."And before La La Land debuted in 2016, Emma joked around about the number of films she's done with Ryan, telling E! News, "He has a restraining order against me now.""Restraining order" aside, Ryan said it was "great to work" with Emma, explaining, "I think it brings the best out of [us] because you know one another, and you are able to help each other in a way that you can't if you're strangers."

Jim and Pam on The Office are one of the most beloved TV couples of all-time, with fans rooting for the Dunder Mifflin employees to be together throughout the NBC hit's nine-year run. Jam's chemistry never transitioned into an off-screen romance between John and Jenna, though she did admit to the pair having "real chemistry" during a 2016 appearance on Watch What Happens Live when a caller asked how close they were."There's like a real part of me that is Pam and a real part of him that's Jim and those parts of us were genuinely in love with one another," Jenna explained. "But in real life we aren't totally Pam and totally Jim, so in real life we're not the perfect match…he was like a type of spouse that I had for a long time, he was my partner and we will always be close because of it."John later weighed in on his costar's headline-making comments, telling The Daily Beast, "I think we both feel it's such an honor to be a part of that relationship. As far as how she was quoted about saying we were 'genuinely in love,' I think that was taken wildly out of context and I feel bad for her."We'll always have the teapot.

Gaga isn't the first co-star Bradley has been romantically linked to in the press, with his onscreen dynamic with Jennifer in movies such as Silver Linings Playbook and American Hustle sparking rumors for years. In fact, Bradley was asked by Howard Stern in 2015, "When are you two gonna have sex? Everyone is waiting for that." Bradley was quick to respond, "Never. It's just not the way we are together."And, at the 2013 Golden Globes, when he was asked by Entertainment Tonight if they were were dating, Bradley responded, "Oh my god. That's very funny. No, my God, no."

They may have costarred in How to Lose a Guy in 10 Days, but the pair gained a rapid number of fans rooting for them to find each other IRL after the 2006 rom-com. But it never happened.In an interview with Howard Stern on his SiriusXM show in October 2020, Matthew revealed it simply never appealed to him to date one of his famous costars."I've always tried to keep it professional and the people I worked with, I must say, did it well," he shared. "Maybe we had certain crushes on each other at certain times but we always just kept it professional."

And with that, the chance for their love to blossom died, just like that love fern.

These A-list best friends have off-the-charts on-screen chemistry (Ocean's Eleven, anyone?) that has extended offscreen in a purely platonic way. Just look at their giggle-filled interviews, gushing public speeches and the fact that George has lent out his coveted Lake Como home to the Roberts-Moder family for anniversary celebrations. NBD!

Along with the ball dropping on New Year's Eve, you can always count on people wondering if the best friends and CNN's Live From Times Square co-hosts have ever dated. When Andy appeared on Howard Stern's radio show, he was asked, "What is it about Anderson Cooper that keeps you from falling in love with him?" The Watch What Happens Live host replied, "I just think it's not what our relationship is based on. We're just friends. That's not a part of it. I think, at this point, we know each other too well. We're not attracted to each other in that way."Funnily enough, the pair first met when they were set up on a blind date over 25 years ago. "You know when straight people know two gay guys, they're like, 'Oh, you guys should meet,'" Anderson said on The Tonight Show in 2017, adding that when the two had a phone call to schedule the date, he "knew within 45 seconds I was never going on a date with Andy Cohen."He explained that Andy "violated" a cardinal rule" when it comes to dating the CNN host: He asked about Anderson's mother, Gloria Vanderbilt. "I wanted to date the Vanderbilt boy!" Andy admitted. "I was excited!"

While Zooey said the pair had "so much fun" making the 2009 indie rom-com (500) Days of Summer, Joseph admitted dating his co-star and longtime friend would be "awkward" in a 2012 interview with Playboy."Zooey and I just think it's funny," he said of fans wanting them to be together. "It is funny. We've been friends for 10 years."

Before it was confirmed that the High School Musical heartthrob was dating his co-star Vanessa Hudgens, there was speculation that he was involved with their mutual best friend Ashley. His 2006 guest appearance as her love interest on The Suite Life of Zack and Cody only fueled the rumors.Zac and Ashley still remain close to this day, with Ashley calling him her "brother/best friend," though she did pick Zac as her worst onscreen kiss in an interview with Elle. "It was the worst because he is like my brother," she explained. "At the time, he was used to acting on Warner Brothers, which is CW, and we were on Disney Channel."She then called him out for trying to kiss her "with his tongue," prompting her to tell him, "'Get away from me!'""I closed my mouth so fast. I was like, 'This is Disney Channel, we don't kiss like that on Disney Channel!'" Ashley recalled. "It's just weird when you're so close to somebody, we'd already done a movie, I'd known him for years before,'" she said. "'That is why it was the worst, it's just we're too close.'"

While their High School Musical characters Chad and Taylor were teen sweethearts, Corbin and Monique left the Disney franchise with a life-long friendship. The duo reunited on-screen in the 2021 Lifetime Christmas movie, A Christmas Dance Reunion, with Corbin writing on Instagram, "After 13 years it felt like coming home working and dancing with [Monique] again. Starring in a [Lifetime] Christmas movie has always been a dream of mine, but never in a million years did I think I'd get to share the screen with one of my favorite people."And Monique is hoping to continue working with "one of her best friends," telling People, "I honestly pray that we get to do more things together because we have that sort of spark that Tom Hanks and Meg Ryan had, and Leo and Kate, and Emma Stone and Ryan Gosling, and all of these different couples that we've seen in movie after movie together. I really feel like we have that potential as well and I'd like to see that happen."

They may have played one of TV's most iconic will-they-or-won't-they couples on The X-Files, but the co-stars actually didn't get along while filming their hit Fox show. In a 2008 interview with Metro UK, David admitted that he often fought with Gillian during the series' initial eight-year run because, "Familiarity breeds contempt. It's nothing to do with the other person. We used to argue about nothing. We couldn't stand the sight of each other."That didn't stop fans from wanting Mulder and Scully to get together, both on-screen and off, with a photo from their May 2021 lunch date going viral, much to David's amusement. "As I was leaving she was like, 'Let's take a photo,'" he told People. "I was told there was a big reaction to it! I never get that stuff, but it's really cool that people are interested after all these years."

Avengers shippers, assemble!While they've appeared in eight movies together since first collaborating on 2004's The Perfect Score, the superhero co-stars have never hooked up IRL. But Scarlett and Chris have developed a deep comfort level with each other over the years. "It's really a result of 10 years of knowing somebody and being able to have a kind of intimacy with them that I think you get from just spending a lot of time with somebody and knowing their soft underbelly," Scarlett explained of their chemistry to Entertainment Weekly in March 2020.

#832. 'Star Trek' star Patrick Stewart dies age 86

The Shakespearean actor landed the role of a lifetime as "Star Trek" Captain Picard. He passed away at age 86.

For Star Trek fans, he was the legendary Captain Picard; the British actor and director Patrick Stewart, longtime member of the  Royal Shakespeare Company, died on Thursday at the age of 86 following a "brief and poignant journey" with Alzheimer's disease and Lewy body dementia, according to an official statement on his social media accounts.

In Los Angeles, California, far away from the small English village of Mirfield where he was born, Stewart achieved world fame. He was 47 years old when he landed the role of a lifetime in the legendary science fiction series Star Trek: Playing Captain Jean-Luc Picard in "Star Trek: The Next Generation," he stepped into the shoes of the legendary Captain James T. Kirk, played by William Shatner.

Stewart brought a calm, measured and distinctly British presence that quickly made Picard a fan favorite and a cult figure in the Star Trek universe. He returned to the role decades later in the spin-off series "Star Trek: Picard," which ended in 2023, proving the character's enduring appeal.

As Captain Jean-Luc Picard, he led the crew of the starship Enterprise, a spaceship with the sizeable mission: "To explore strange new worlds. To seek out new life and new civilizations" — and most importantly, "to boldly go where no man has gone before!"

Stewart's interest in acting was sparked in the early 1950s when a teacher asked him to recite a work by Shakespeare. His passion for Shakespeare stayed with him until the end.

His parents were far removed from the glamor of the theatrical world. His father was a highly respected officer in the British Army during World War II, but at home, he was an abusive husband, and young Patrick had to helplessly witness repeated violence against his mother. Stewart wrote about his experiences with domestic violence in The Guardian in 2009. The stage, he confessed there, seemed to him "a far safer place" than reality; he saw acting as a way to escape his home life.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Patrick began acting at the age of 12. At 16, he left school early and, thanks to a scholarship, studied acting in Bristol, England. Along the way, he worked as a journalist. In 1965, he became an official member of the Royal Shakespeare Company, and remained with the theather company from 1966 to 1982. Such was his passion for the great English playwright and lyricist that he even shared his sonnets on his Twitter account during the 2020 coronavirus pandemic.

Stewart dazzled the theater world with his own stage adaptation of Charles Dickens' 1843 tale "A Christmas Carol." He played more than 30 roles himself. After its 1987 premiere in Stewart's hometown of Mirfield, the one-man show became a critics' favorite and a long-running hit on Broadway in New York.

In the same year,  Stewart went from being a stage actor to an international TV star. Star Trek producer Robert Justman offered him the role of Captain Jean-Luc Picard, one of the main characters in a new edition of the popular TV series "Star Trek: The Next Generation."

The successful Shakespearean hesitated. Until then, he had never worked in Hollywood. But his agent encouraged him to accept the role, Stewart recalled in a 2020 interview with the German newspaper Die Welt. "You can accept the offer as a start for now. It won't be a big deal, you can't revive a series as iconic as Star Trek anyway."

But his agent was to be proven wrong: Stewart led the Starship Enterprise through its galactic adventures for seven seasons and four full-length feature films. The TV series had astronomical success on Earth in a very short time. At first, the producers were at odds as to whether Stewart's British accent could really fit the role of commander of a US starship in the 24th century, but it soon became impossible to imagine the series without the subtly diplomatic Captain Picard, who often quoted Shakespeare while at the helm. It seemed as if all the time he had spent as a Shakespearean actor had prepared him to command the Enterprise, Stewart once remarked with a wink. When the cult series ended in 1994, he had ruled out ever returning to the Enterprise's command center.

In 2010, the actor was knighted by the Queen of England. Stewart considered it the greatest honor of his career to stand alongside acting greats such as Sir Laurence Olivier and Sir Alec Guinness.

Beyond the screen, Stewart has long used his voice for social and human rights causes. In recent years, he has drawn attention to issues such as violence against women, age discrimination and the protection of children.

In a June 2020 interview, "Playboy" asked the New York resident whether he was considering retiring from acting. "Never! That would mean giving up my life," replied Stewart, who was approaching his 80th birthday at the time. He was filming the second of three seasons of "Star Trek: Picard." The series ends with a final episode in which the retired Starfleet admiral makes his last appearance. In the series, Picard retires to his family vineyard in France but is drawn back into space to confront new threats to the Federation.

This series also showcases Stewart's affection for his pit bull, Ginger. In "Star Trek: Picard," Picard also has a pit bull, a loyal four-legged companion named Number One — a deliberate reference to Stewart's real-life love of the breed. For his efforts to combat prejudice against pit bulls and to support their adoption, Stewart was honored by the US animal welfare organization ASPCA, among others.

In 2024, he published his memoir "Making it So." In it, he recounts his passion for theater and his love of Shakespeare.

Now, at the age of 86, the British actor has finally departed for another galaxy. Farewell, Patrick Stewart!

#831. Kane beat Mbappe to Ballon d'Or by just 28 points

'My heart was beating so fast' - Kane wins Ballon D'or

Harry Kane beat second-placed Kylian Mbappe to the men's Ballon d'Or by just 28 points - one of the smallest winning margins in the award's history.

Organisers released voting numbers on Saturday, showing that England captain Kane was awarded 1,055 points, compared with 1,027 for Real Madrid's France forward Mbappe.

Bayern Munich striker Kane became the first Englishman to win the award since Michael Owen in 2001, while France talisman Mbappe also claimed his best finish, ending up well clear of Spain forward Lamine Yamal, who was third with 881 points.

It was the smallest winning margin since Argentina great Lionel Messi beat Liverpool defender Virgil van Dijk by seven points in 2019, while the men's Ballon d'Or has twice been decided by a single point.

That happened when England World Cup winner Bobby Charlton, who was later knighted, beat Portugal star Eusebio by the smallest possible margin in 1966, and Germany defender Matthias Sammer repeated the tight one-point victory when he edged out Brazil striker Ronaldo in 1996.

Mbappe may take heart from Ronaldo's Ballon d'Or experience as the legendary frontman, who presented Kane with his award in London on Monday, went on to win in 1997 and again in 2002.

Harry Kane is the fifth English player to win the Ballon d'Or, after Stanley Matthews (1956), Bobby Charlton (1966), Kevin Keegan (1978 & 1979) and Michael Owen (2001)

Kane clinched the prize after scoring 73 goals in 65 matches last season, helping Bayern Munich to a league and cup double and leading England to a third-place finish at the World Cup.

The award is decided by votes from 100 journalists, using a weighted points system.

Speaking about Mbappe missing out on the award, Real Madrid head coach Jose Mourinho said the 27-year-old was dealing brilliantly with the disappointment.

"Kylian is very intelligent and mature. He has very high self-esteem. And at the same time, he has class," Mourinho said before Real's game against Racing Santander on Sunday in La Liga.

"The way he handled the Ballon d'Or for Harryâ¦ all I saw and felt was class. And respect.

"It's one thing to know you're the best, and another to have respect for someone who has also worked hard to win a trophy. All I see in him is class."

#829. Collins English Dictionary Names "Mogging" 2026 Word of the Year

“Mogging” was crowned Collins English Dictionary’s 2026 Word of the Year—here’s why.

“Mogging” is mogging extra hard right now.

After all, the slang word—coined by Gen Z and Gen Alpha—has been named the Collins English Dictionary’s 2026 Word of the Year.

“BREAKING NEWS The Collins Word of the Year is…mogging,” the dictionary announced on their official Instagram page Nov. 3. “Although the word has been around since the 2010s, it has now been firmly adopted by Gen Z and Gen Alpha in a playful and ironic way when someone is upstaged.”

According to the Collins English Dictionary, “mogging” is a noun defined as “the act of outshining or outperforming someone or something.”

So, in case it’s still not clear, Beyoncé was absolutely mogging when she arrived at the 2026 Met Gala in a crystal-embellished, skeleton-inspired gown. Tate McRae strutting on the 2026 Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show runway after her performance? Mogging.

And who could forget when Alysa Liu said her “main goal for this competition was to mog” shortly after her performance at the 2026 Milano Cortina Winter Olympics? Living up to her objective, the 21-year-old scored two gold medals during the games.

Describing the term as a “fast-growing slang word,” the Collins English Dictionary honored “mogging” with its number one spot this year because experts found there was a 210% increase in usage in 2026, the organization shared.

“‘Mogging’ has firmly entered mainstream language this year,” they explained, “becoming widely used online and a part of everyday conversation among younger generations.”

And while younger generations can take credit for the word’s rise in popularity, its origins span back to 2016.

In fact, it was derived from the phrase AMOG (Alpha Male of the Group), the Collins English Dictionary wrote on their Language Lovers blog, a noun initially used in bodybuilding culture “for the most physically dominant man in the gym.”

“Fast forward to 2026 and it’s everywhere,” the blog continued. “Teenagers mog elite athletes, a new video game mogs an old favorite, and your friend’s sourdough mogs the loaf you spent all weekend proving.”

And now, “mogging” is truly outshining all other words this year.

“The selection of 'mogging’ as Collins’ Word of the Year shows how each generation leaves its mark on language,” Collins managing director Alex Beecroft shared in a statement. “It’s a great example of how Gen Z and Gen Alpha have adopted a word and turned it into humorous slang, making the language their own and ‘mogging’ the rest of us!”’

#828. Worst in the EFL - the team with a penalty problem

Shaquille Gwengwe is among several Newport players to miss from the penalty spot

While fans would normally celebrate their team earning a penalty, Newport County supporters could be forgiven for putting their heads in their hands.

With three-quarters of penalties successfully converted, on average, earning a spot kick would normally be reason to celebrate.

Not so for Newport where anticipation has been replaced by apprehension.

Across the past two seasons, they have converted just two of nine penalties in all competitions - and only one of six in League Two.

Their 16.7% conversion rate is the worst in the entire English Football League (EFL).

And for a team just two points off the play-offs, missed penalties could prove costly.

Three different managers and several players have tried to find the formula, but the outcome has remained remarkably similar.

There was hope Harrison Biggins had ended the slump when he netted from the spot in a draw at Rotherham in October.

Four days later, that optimism evaporated.

The midfielder stepped up against Cheltenham Town but, having chosen the same side, saw his effort saved in the 1-0 defeat.

Manager Hayden Mullins refused to blame Biggins after his miss at Cheltenham and, having done the job himself as a player, has sympathy.

"We never lay any blame on anyone who steps up to take a penalty," said the 47-year-old.

"Penalties are always tough. Harrison scored the game before [but] it's a game of cat and mouse really between you and the goalkeeper.

"You don't know what the goalkeeper is thinking, all you can do is pick a side and execute it with aggression."

Dibley-Dias to miss County's game against Chesterfield

Exiles' Mullins not given enough credit - Jenkins

While a player may not be able to predict a goalkeeper's thought process, recent penalties may have handed Stanway a clue.

Six of Newport's last nine penalties have been aimed to the right and - on each occasion - the keeper has guessed correctly with Cameron Antwi, Nathaniel Opoku, Bobby Kamwa and Shaquille Gwengwe all denied. Only Biggins' effort at Rotherham found the net.

Even when Newport altered their approach, the result was often no different.

Ged Garner was denied to the left against Swindon Town and Yahya Bamba - aiming for the top corner - saw his effort ruled out for a double touch.

Bamba converted the retake by waiting for the goalkeeper to move, a method similar to manager Mullins' own approach during his midfield days with Crystal Palace, West Ham and Portsmouth.

"I know how hard it is. Everyone's got their own technique," said Mullins.

"I would run up, have one eye on the goalkeeper and whichever way he went, I would go the other way, but it's brave."

Newport County have the worst conversion rate from the spot in the entire EFL

It begs the question whether or not Newport practice penalties.

They have not always struggled from the spot and between 2023 and 2025, scored 10 of 13 between forwards Will Evans and Omar Bogle.

Mullins prefers to hand sole responsibility to to his centre-forward but has been without Shaquille Gwenge through suspension for the past three games - during which Newport have missed two penalties - since missing from the spot himself.

Gwenge is available again and Mullins insisted the striker - with six goals already this season - practices penalties "for a long time" after training.

But the County boss says he would "never spend too much energy" worrying about the miserable success rate.

"Penalties are down to a lot of things - fatigue, mindset, where you are, who you're taking it in front of, how you feel at that time and who you're up against," he said.

"We can look at it and practice as much as we can.

"We'll be ready for the next time we take it and hopefully it goes our way."
